articles.title: Open tenders have ended cartels, will boost finances: Finance Minister in TN budget
articles.description: Tamil Nadu's Finance Minister N Marie Wilson announced major public procurement reforms. These changes aim to end cartelisation and improve transparency in government contracts. Unnecessary certification requirements for contractors have been removed, allowing wider participation. Building approval powers were delegated to the CMDA, eliminating corruption in that process. These measures will strengthen state finances through efficiency and better value for public spending.

articles.title: ALMM-II: MNRE Exempts Select Solar Projects Based on Bid, Commissioning Timelines
articles.description: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) has issued detailed clarifications on the applicability of the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) List-II for solar photovoltaic (PV) cells, providing greater certainty to developers across utility-scale, rooftop, behind-the-meter (BTM) and government solar projects. In an Office Memorandum, the ministry said the clarification follows multiple representations seeking guidance on the implementation of ALMM List-II for solar PV cells after its July 18, 2026 notification. Provision For Bids Before Aug, 2025 For projects awarded through competitive bidding, MNRE said those with the last date of bid submission on or before August 31, 2025 will remain exempt from the requirement to use ALMM-listed solar PV cells. Projects with bid submission deadlines after August 31, 2025, however, will have to comply with ALMM List-II. The ministry also clarified that tenders with bid submission dates between December 9, 2024 and July 28, 2025 will continue to be governed by their original bid conditions. It said its Office Memorandum issued on July 28, 2025, which shifted the ALMM List-II applicability cut-off to August 31, 2025, does not automatically alter conditions contained in existing tender documents. For Net-Metering & Open Access Projects For net-metering and open-access projects, MNRE said projects commissioned by December 31, 2026 will be exempt from ALMM List-II for solar PV cells. The exemption applies irrespective of whether the project was initiated before or after July 18, 2026 and does not require any prior approval. However, compliance with ALMM List-I for solar PV modules will continue wherever applicable. The clarification also extends to residential rooftop installations under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana. Residential consumers availing net metering under the scheme will remain exempt from ALMM List-II for solar PV cells until March 31, 2027, provided applications are submitted through the PMSG National Portal. The requirement to use ALMM-listed solar PV modules, however, will continue to apply. For Rooftop Solar Projects For rooftop solar projects on government buildings awarded through bidding, MNRE has prescribed separate treatment based on bid timelines. Projects with bid submission dates on or before December 9, 2024 will remain exempt from ALMM List-II. Projects with bid deadlines between December 9, 2024 and July 28, 2025 will continue to be governed by their tender conditions, while those with bid deadlines between July 28 and August 31, 2025 will also remain exempt. Projects where bids closed after August 31, 2025 will be required to use ALMM-listed solar PV cells. For government rooftop projects not awarded through bidding, projects commissioned by December 31, 2026 will be exempt from ALMM List-II for solar PV cells. Those commissioned after that date will have to use ALMM-listed cells. Behind The Meter Projects The ministry also clarified the position for behind-the-meter (BTM) projects. It said ALMM List-I for modules and ALMM List-II for cells will not apply to captive BTM solar projects developed by private consumers or groups of consumers, excluding government entities and public sector enterprises (PSEs). For captive BTM projects developed by government entities and PSEs, projects commissioned by December 31, 2026 will be required to use ALMM-listed solar PV modules but will remain exempt from using ALMM-listed solar PV cells. Projects commissioned after that date will have to use both ALMM-listed modules and ALMM-listed cells. MNRE also clarified that the latest Office Memorandum does not affect Domestic Content Requirement (DCR) provisions applicable under various government schemes. It said DCR obligations will continue to be governed by the respective scheme guidelines, and the ALMM clarification does not dilute requirements relating to domestically manufactured solar PV modules or cells wherever DCR norms are applicable.

articles.title: Gujarat govt imposes statewide ban on glue traps, citing animal cruelty
articles.description: Gandhinagar, Aug 4 (IANS) The Gujarat government has imposed an immediate statewide ban on the production, sale, storage and use of glue traps, commonly known as sticky boards, used to catch rats and other small animals, making the devices illegal across the state as part of a move to prevent cruelty to animals. The decision was announced through a resolution issued by the state's Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department. The ban applies to the manufacture, sale, purchase, storage and use of glue traps with immediate effect. Glue traps are coated with a highly adhesive, non-drying substance that immobilises animals and birds on contact. According to the government, trapped animals often sustain serious injuries while attempting to escape and may eventually die from starvation, dehydration, suffocation or injuries caused during their struggle. The government said the use of glue traps violates Section 11(1) of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960. It also noted that the Animal Welfare Board of India has classified the use of glue traps as highly cruel and illegal under its guidelines. In a parallel measure, the Industries and Mines Department has directed that glue traps be removed with immediate effect from the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) procurement portal as well as from other e-commerce and online platforms. The order also prohibits all government departments, boards, corporations and local self-government bodies from purchasing or using the devices. The resolution warns that any violation of the ban may attract legal action under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, and Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, along with any other applicable provisions of law. District Police authorities and the Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (SPCA) have been authorised to register complaints and initiate action against those found violating the prohibition. The government has directed traders to immediately stop stocking and selling glue traps, as their production, sale, purchase and storage are now prohibited. It has also advised members of the public not to use glue traps for rodent control in homes, offices or factories. Instead, citizens have been encouraged to adopt legally approved and animal-friendly alternatives, including cage traps and other non-lethal rodent control methods, in place of adhesive traps. --IANS mys/dan
